import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Wolstenholme Prime

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolstenholme_prime)
-/


namespace WolstenholmePrime

/--
Wolstenholme's theorem states that any prime $p > 3$ satisfies $\binom{2p-1}{p-1} \equiv 1 (\pmod{p^3})$.

Formal proof linked here provided by AlphaProof.
*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolstenholme%27s_theorem)
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/d833ed31d82693f10bed7a4c9ac329545b556a03/FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/WolstenholmePrime.lean#L34"]
theorem wolstenholme_theorem (p : ℕ) (h : p > 3) (hp : Nat.Prime p) :
    (2 * p - 1).choose (p - 1) ≡ 1 [MOD p ^ 3] := by
  sorry


/--
A prime $p > 7$ is called a *Wolstenholme prime* if $\binom{2p-1}{p-1} \equiv 1 (\pmod{p^4})$.
-/
def IsWolstenholmePrime (p : ℕ) : Prop :=
  p > 7 ∧ p.Prime ∧ (2 * p - 1).choose (p - 1) ≡ 1 [MOD p ^ 4]

/--
Two known Wolstenholme primes: 16843 and 2124679.

Formal proof linked here provided by AlphaProof
-/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem wolstenholme_prime_16483 : IsWolstenholmePrime 16843 := by
  unfold IsWolstenholmePrime Nat.ModEq
  refine ⟨by norm_num, by norm_num, ?_⟩
  native_decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem wolstenholme_prime_2124679 : IsWolstenholmePrime 2124679 := by
  unfold IsWolstenholmePrime Nat.ModEq
  refine ⟨by norm_num, by norm_num, ?_⟩
  native_decide

/--
Equivalently, a prime $p > 7$ is a Wolstenholme prime if it divides the numerator of the Bernoulli number $B_{p-3}$.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem wolstenholme_bernoulli (p : ℕ) : IsWolstenholmePrime p ↔
    (p > 7) ∧ Nat.Prime p ∧ ↑p ∣ (bernoulli' (p - 3)).num := by
  sorry

/--
Another equivalent definition is that a prime $p > 7$ is a Wolstenholme prime
if it $p^3$ divides the numerator of the harmonic number $H_{p-1}$.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem wolstenholme_harmonic (p : ℕ) : IsWolstenholmePrime p ↔
    (p > 7) ∧ Nat.Prime p ∧ ↑(p ^ 3) ∣ (harmonic (p - 1)).num := by
  sorry

/--
It is conjectured that there are infinitely many Wolstenholme primes.

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolstenholme_prime#Expected_number_of_Wolstenholme_primes)
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem wolstenholme_prime_infinite :
    {p : ℕ | IsWolstenholmePrime p}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end WolstenholmePrime

reformulations.difference: The explicit p > 7 cutoff matches the main Wikipedia article, but is absent from the definition on the cited Wolstenholme's theorem page and from the primary paper's odd-prime definition.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The primes at most 7 are 2, 3, 5, and 7. Their binomial coefficients are respectively 3, 10, 126, and 1716, none congruent to 1 modulo p^4. Thus the cutoff excludes no qualifying prime. Review.cutoff_equiv proves the pointwise equivalence in scratch.lean, and Review.infinitude_cutoff_equiv proves that the infinitude statement is unchanged. Neither proof uses the file's admitted theorems.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses bernoulli', whose B₁ is +1/2, whereas the primary source uses the conventional generating function z/(exp(z)-1), corresponding to Mathlib's bernoulli with B₁ = -1/2.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The two sequences agree at every index other than 1. Under p > 7, p - 3 is not 1, so the rational numbers and their reduced numerators are identical. Review.bernoulli_statement_equiv proves the equivalence of the full characterization statements in scratch.lean without using the admitted characterization theorem.

review.notes: All seven mathematical declarations were checked; no misformalization was found. Rat.num supplies the reduced integer numerator, both divisibility conditions are in ℤ, and harmonic (p - 1) sums the reciprocals from 1 through p - 1. Zero and small-prime cases cause no unintended behavior. Lean tests passed for the classical theorem and harmonic characterization for p < 40, and the Bernoulli characterization for p < 16. Independent modular-product computations also confirmed primality and the defining congruence for 16843 and 2124679. The current Wikipedia source still records infinitude as conjectural. Experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/known_tests.lean. The external AlphaProof artifact was not audited because its link points into a formal-conjectures GitHub fork, which was avoided under the access prohibition; the mathematical statement of wolstenholme_theorem was independently verified against the sources.
